title: "032 — Test suite tiering"

## 032 — Test suite tiering {#sec-032}

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Audit and refactor the test suite into three explicit, enforced tiers so
feedback arrives at the speed its claim deserves: pure logic and server handlers run
in-process in Node, component behavior renders in a real browser without the full
stack, and end-to-end tests shrink to the few flows that genuinely need the real
browser, server, streaming, and persistence. The audit found the suite reporting
coverage it did not have: 186 unit/integration files, 32 "component" or "route" files
that read `.svelte` source with the filesystem and asserted on text, no real
component-rendering tier, and a 37-case Playwright suite that was serialized, replayed
onboarding before every test, and contained fixed-duration waits.

**Why.** The daily inner loop paid browser and full-stack costs for claims that could
be proved in milliseconds, while component interaction went unverified or was pushed
into the slowest tier. The cost compounded in CI: a serialized end-to-end deck with
per-test setup made every release candidate slower than the product changes it guarded.
The feature's bet was that placement, not tooling, was the problem — a test belongs to
the lowest tier that can prove its claim, and the suite should make that choice obvious
and machine-enforced.

**Outcome & reversals.** The suite now has three named tiers with distinct suffixes and
commands: Tier 1 (`*.test.ts`, `pnpm test:unit`), Tier 2 (`*.browser.test.ts`, real
Chromium through Vitest, `pnpm test:browser`), and Tier 3 (`tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`,
Playwright, `pnpm test:e2e`). `pnpm test` remains the local merge gate over Tiers 1+2.
The obvious Tier 2 suffix, `*.svelte.test.ts`, was rejected because it already meant a
`.svelte.ts` rune-module test and had to stay in Tier 1; the browser tier took
`*.browser.test.ts` instead. All 32 source-text files were classified in a migration
ledger as convert (28), promote-static (3), or retain (1); the 28 converted files were
replaced by real render/interaction tests and then deleted, with three deliberate
production breaks proving the replacements fail when the behavior is broken. Component
network calls moved to MSW at the `fetch` boundary, with shared handlers and a worker
asset served only by the test Vite server.

Tier 3 was pruned rather than parallelized into respectability: 29 cases after the
telemetry spec retired dropped to 8 cases across 6 specs, a 72% reduction, with every
removal mapped to lower-tier coverage or a recorded retirement rationale. Onboarding
and auth state are captured once in `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts` and consumed through the
shared session fixture; third-party traffic is blocked deterministically; the sharded
suite went from two shards to four. The telemetry end-to-end flow was retired outright
rather than made shard-safe — its protocol coverage moved to a Tier 1 ingest test and a
Tier 2 client-emission test, freeing the suite from the external langfuse-stub port.
Parallelism is capability-gated: at least 8 logical CPUs and 8 GiB usable RAM (host and
cgroup minimum) enables parallel execution, while low-spec or unreadable hardware runs
serially; the gate changes concurrency, never test selection.

Guardrails and budgets closed the loop. `scripts/check-test-tiers.mjs` implements
`TT-001`–`TT-008` for browser imports in Tier 1, fixed waits and setup replay in Tier 3,
source-text component assertions, missing session fixtures, ungated concurrency, full-stack
dependencies in Tier 2, and accidental inclusion of integration tests; each rule was
verified by injecting a scratch violation and restoring the tree. CI runs `pnpm test:ci`
and `pnpm test:e2e:ci` per shard, writes tier duration reports, and fails a job that
exceeds `test-budgets.json` (60 s Tier 1, 120 s Tier 2, 120 s per Tier 3 shard, 120 s
server). jsdom was deliberately retained: four Tier 1 files still select it for pure DOM
algorithms (`auth/state`, `markdown/focusable`, `settings/hash-sync`, `utils/media`), and
those tests are Node DOM emulation, not the browser tier.

**Learnings.**

- Placement is the lever: the same assertions became fast or slow depending on which
  layer proved them, and naming the tiers made the wrong choice visible in review.
- A suffix is an interface. Reusing `.svelte.test.ts` for browser tests would have
  silently reclassified rune-module tests; the awkward new suffix was cheaper than
  ambiguity.
- Source-text tests are worse than no tests at the component tier because they report
  coverage that cannot fail when the rendered behavior breaks. Converting them required
  proving the new test fails first.
- End-to-end pruning is a coverage exercise, not a deletion exercise: every removed case
  needed a lower-tier owner or an explicit retirement rationale in the ledger.
- Hardware assumptions belong in one gate. The same threshold now drives Vitest,
  Playwright, and the shard scripts, so local guidance and CI behavior cannot drift.
